properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is chosen.

ANTHONY, 2026-09-23, in his own words: "What I was thinking would be nice for somebody to just publish requirements (in reflow2 graph form). For instance, my brother wants to build a shop in Kennewick, WA. Maybe a template for building a shop in Kennewick WA could be just the requirements for building a shop. Then my brother just uploads the requirements template and builds whatever he likes (as long as it meets all the requirements of a shop in Kennewick)." He tied it to the templates idea and to the x-dimension discussion of 2026-09-22.

⭐⭐ WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT "TEMPLATE", AND IT IS THE WHOLE CONTENT OF THE IDEA. The template ideas recorded so far (`dec:idea-a-domain-seed-template-starts-a-design-in-the-fields-own-shape`, `dec:idea-an-org-template-carries-the-approved-references-a-design-must-use`) are about a SEED: structure copied into a new design, which the user then owns and edits. This one is the opposite kind of thing: OBLIGATIONS the user does NOT own and cannot edit — only satisfy. The publisher says WHAT must hold; the brother decides HOW (post-frame or stick-built, one bay or three) and the design is judged only on whether every published requirement is met. That is solution-neutral requirements, which is the systems-engineering meaning of a requirement in the first place.

⭐⭐ AND reflow2 ALREADY HAS THE VOCABULARY FOR EXACTLY THIS, WITH THIS EXACT CITY IN IT. `dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built` records the founding operating-environment document (2026-07-17): "A house in Kennewick WA must meet city ordinances, county rules, state requirements, building and fire codes, seismic provisions and occupancy limits". Its schema keeps three kinds of rule apart, and the third is this idea precisely: `Constraint` is self-imposed, `DesignRule` is a chosen convention, and `EnvironmentRule` is EXTERNALLY IMPOSED — "the design cannot negotiate it, only comply, seek a variance, or fail". The shapes are all declared: `Project OPERATES_IN Environment`, `Environment IMPOSES EnvironmentRule`, `COMPLIES_WITH` / `VIOLATES_RULE`, with a confirmed violation standing for an accepted variance. The half that locates a design (`Environment`, `DEPLOYED_TO`) is built; the compliance half never was, and `decision:vocab:environment` parks it "deliberately unused until a user asks for it". ⇒ THIS IS THE FIRST TIME A REAL USER HAS ASKED, with a real site and a real builder. The parking note said a real request should pull it back in.

⭐ AND IT IS THE x-DIMENSION WITH A PUBLISHER WHO IS NOT THE BUILDER. `dec:idea-design-is-composable-on-two-axes-authority-and-role` defines x as one design holding intent and others each holding a realisation of it, and sharpens it to "design is not always the same users" (A5 writes requirements; others build to them). A Kennewick shop template is that axis in plain form: the city, or whoever transcribes its rules, is the requirements organisation; the brother is the one implementation; a neighbour building a different shop is a rival implementation of the same requirements, comparable on the same denominator.

📌 AND THE JURISDICTIONS STACK, which puts the y-axis back in. A shop in Kennewick answers to more than one publisher at once: the city, the county, the state's adopted building code, and possibly the utility and a homeowners' association. Those publishers form an authority hierarchy of their own. So the example again touches both axes: the brother's design SATISFIES across x, and what it satisfies is a stack ordered down y. (Illustrative: which bodies actually impose what on a Kennewick shop is NOT checked here, and must not be read as a statement of the code.)

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.

(a) REFERENCE, NOT COPY. The requirements live in the publisher's own design, marked published; the brother's design declares a pinned dependency on it (`external_dependency` / `mirrors`, "designed against your published surface at this version") and satisfies those requirements from his side. When the publisher revises, his design learns it from the pin. ⚠️ Blocked today by the same missing piece as both axes: SATISFIES cannot cross a graph boundary (`create_edge` resolves both endpoints in scope), `export_surface` carries no Verifications, `mirror_surface`'s refresh is recorded as broken, and reflow2 itself publishes 0 of its own requirements.

(b) COPY IN, WITH A PIN. `/genesis` (or `import_graph` / `merge_designs`) brings the published requirements into the brother's own design, marked with a provenance that can never read as his own word (the seed-template node already noted `provenance: imported` as the hook) and pinned to the template version, so a later version can be compared (`compare_designs`) and the difference offered to him. Works with what exists today, and within one graph SATISFIES, verification and closure all work. ⚠️ Counter: a copy is a second home for the publisher's facts — the one-fact-one-home problem the hub work named — and it goes stale silently unless the pin is read.

(c) THE REQUIREMENTS ARRIVE AS ENVIRONMENT RULES. The template is an Environment ("Kennewick, WA") that IMPOSES EnvironmentRules; the brother's Project OPERATES_IN it; compliance is recorded per rule as COMPLIES_WITH or VIOLATES_RULE (a confirmed violation being a variance). This builds the parked layer and uses its variance lifecycle, which is better thought through than much of what ships. It composes with (a) or (b) as to WHERE the rules live. ⚠️ Counter: it splits "requirements" in two — a builder's own requirements and the imposed ones behave differently — which is the point, but is a second concept a user has to learn.

(d) THE SIMPLEST THING: A REQUIREMENTS-ONLY DESIGN, SHARED AS A FILE. Somebody writes "shop in Kennewick" as an ordinary reflow2 design with Requirements and no build, publishes the export, and the brother imports it as the start of his. No new mechanism at all; the question becomes only how to tell imported requirements from his own. Closest to how he described it ("uploads the requirements template"), and the cheapest experiment that would show whether the rest is needed.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea rather than used against it:

🛑 CODES ARE CONDITIONAL, AND A FLAT LIST WILL NOT SERVE. Real building rules apply only if the design crosses a threshold (floor area, height, use, occupancy, distance to a property line). A template that states every rule unconditionally either buries the builder or is wrong; one that states applicability has to evaluate it against his design. So a requirement needs an "applies when" that reads the design, and nothing in reflow2 models applicability today.

🛑 AUTHORITY. The city's code is the law; a reflow2 template is somebody's transcription of it. "My design meets the Kennewick shop template" is not "my design will get a permit", and the gap between those is exactly `dec:idea-who-warrants-a-domain-template-and-how-does-it-stay-current`: who wrote it, from which edition, and how a design learns the code changed. A transcription that reads as authoritative is the dangerous kind.

🛑 SCALE AND WHO MAINTAINS IT. Adopted building codes are very large. The realistic first template is small and hand-picked (setbacks, height, permit triggers, the few structural and electrical rules a shop meets), which is useful and must say it is partial, or a builder reads "met all of them" as "met the code".

⚠️ AND THE STANDING OVER-DESIGN WARNING, which is Anthony's own: option (d) needs nothing built, and the first real Kennewick shop would say which of (a)–(c) is actually needed.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SHARPENED 2026-09-23 — THE LONG-TERM FORM: THE OFFICIAL SOURCE PUBLISHES, AND reflow2 ENSURES EVERY REQUIREMENT IS SATISFIED
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING. Anthony, the same day, stating where this goes.

HIS WORDS: "The long term idea would be that an official source (like a city or government office or a standards publisher, etc) can publish all the official requirements for given topic. Then people can just download the reflow2 design graph for that and build to it. Reflow2 should ensure that every requirement is satisfied."

⭐⭐ THIS ANSWERS THE STRONGEST COUNTER ABOVE, THE ONE ABOUT AUTHORITY. That counter was that a template is somebody's TRANSCRIPTION of the law. If the city, the state office or the standards body publishes the graph itself, the publisher IS the authority and there is no transcription to go stale. `dec:idea-who-warrants-a-domain-template-and-how-does-it-stay-current` asked who warrants a template; here the answer is its own author. reflow2's job narrows to CARRYING the warrant faithfully (who published it, which edition, pinned), never issuing one — which is the report-don't-judge posture it already holds.

⭐ AND IT CHOOSES AMONG THE OPTIONS, OR AT LEAST LEANS. An official source revises its requirements (a new code edition, an amended ordinance), so the builder's design must keep pointing at the publisher's version rather than holding a private copy. That is option (a), reference-not-copy with a pin, and the pin is more than a convenience here: which edition governs a building is a legal fact (typically the one in force when the permit was applied for). Option (b), copy-with-pin, would still work for the download, provided the pin is kept and the copy can never read as the builder's own words. Option (d) remains the cheapest first experiment.

⭐⭐ "reflow2 SHOULD ENSURE THAT EVERY REQUIREMENT IS SATISFIED" — WHAT reflow2 CAN HONESTLY ENSURE, AND WHAT IT CANNOT. Much of this machinery exists and is built:
  · `detect_gaps` raises `unsatisfied_requirement` on any requirement nothing SATISFIES;
  · delivery is COMPUTED, never typed: satisfied AND realized AND a passing check;
  · `closure_report` and `coverage_report` say which requirements have a satisfier and which have evidence.
So reflow2 can ensure that EVERY PUBLISHED REQUIREMENT IS ACCOUNTED FOR: each one has something in the builder's design claiming to meet it, and a check whose result is recorded, and nothing is silently skipped. What it cannot ensure is that the shop, as built, really meets the code. That judgement belongs to whoever checks (the city's inspector, a structural engineer), and in reflow2 it arrives as a Verification: method `inspection`, result recorded. The honest wording of the goal is therefore "no requirement can go unaccounted for, and every claim of meeting one carries its evidence", not "reflow2 certifies compliance".

⭐ AND IT CLOSES THE REVERSE CHANNEL IN THE x-AXIS NODE, NAMED "TOSS IT OVER THE FENCE". The city publishes requirements forward; the builder's design, showing each one satisfied with its evidence, is exactly what a permit submission is — the same graph going BACK to the publisher. That is the missing reverse channel `dec:idea-design-is-composable-on-two-axes-authority-and-role` named from Anthony's Air Force experience, in a setting where it already exists on paper (plans submitted, inspections recorded). ⚠️ And it hits the measured blocker again: `export_surface` carries NO Verifications, so the evidence is precisely the part of a design that cannot cross to another design today.

📌 WHAT THIS NEEDS THAT IS NOT THERE, beyond the cross-graph SATISFIES already named:
  · PROVENANCE OF THE PUBLISHER THAT CAN BE CHECKED. If "the City of Kennewick" is only a name in a file, anyone can publish a graph wearing it. Official publication needs a way to verify who published a graph (a signature, or a known location the publisher controls). Without it this is an impersonation hazard, not a feature.
  · APPLICABILITY, as above: official requirements are full of "applies when", and an official source would expect them evaluated, not flattened.
  · A WAY TO DISCOVER what has been published for a place and topic — the download step assumes the builder can find the city's graph.

⚠️ THE SCALE NOTE, recorded because this is a vision for the whole ecosystem and the evidence is one brother's shop: nothing here requires any city to adopt reflow2's format, and none has. (Efforts to publish rules in machine-readable form exist in some governments, under names like "rules as code"; that has not been researched here and is not asserted as a fit.) The first step that proves anything is still one real requirements graph and one real build against it.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SHARPENED 2026-09-23 — THE SAME SHAPE IN PROCUREMENT: A SOLICITATION IS A PUBLISHED REQUIREMENTS GRAPH, AND EACH BID IS A RIVAL DESIGN AGAINST IT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING. Anthony, extending the idea.

HIS WORDS: "This could be expanded to soliciting for proposals. Say a company or government wants somebody to submit bids for a contract. They could post their requirements for the contract on something like sam.gov. then a person could just design/build directly to requirements."

⭐⭐ THIS IS THE x-AXIS WITH MORE THAN ONE IMPLEMENTATION, WHICH IS WHERE IT WAS STRONGEST. The x-axis node argued that x's best property is that rival implementations are COMPARABLE: several designs satisfying one requirements graph can be measured on a shared denominator, which is an Analysis of Alternatives. A solicitation is exactly that: one buyer publishes the requirements, many bidders each submit a design against them, and the buyer compares. The city-permit case had one builder per requirement set; this has many, competing.

⭐ WHAT THE DISCIPLINE ALREADY DOES BY HAND, AND WHAT reflow2 WOULD COMPUTE. A proposal team for a US government solicitation typically builds a COMPLIANCE MATRIX: every "shall" in the solicitation mapped to where the proposal answers it, so the evaluator can see nothing was missed. A buyer's evaluator does the same in reverse. That matrix is a requirements-to-satisfier trace kept by hand in a spreadsheet, and it is the thing reflow2 computes rather than stores: `unsatisfied_requirement`, closure and coverage reports. ⇒ The narrowest honest version of the feature is "the compliance matrix is derived from the design, not maintained beside it". (The solicitation layout usually cited is the Uniform Contract Format — the work statement, the instructions to offerors, and the evaluation factors in separate sections; that is recalled, not researched here.)

WHAT PROCUREMENT ADDS THAT THE PERMIT CASE DID NOT:

  · MANDATORY vs EVALUATED. A solicitation mixes pass/fail requirements ("shall") with things that are SCORED (evaluation factors, relative weights, best value vs lowest price). reflow2 can say every mandatory requirement is accounted for. Scoring is the buyer's judgement and must stay the buyer's — reflow2 can carry the stated factors and weights and lay the bids side by side on them (`analyze_alternatives`, `compare_designs`), never pick the winner.

  · AMENDMENTS AND QUESTIONS. Solicitations are amended, and questions from bidders are answered to everyone. That is the edition pin again (a bid is against amendment N, and must acknowledge each one), plus reflow2's Question/answer records — a bidder's question and the buyer's published answer are the same shape as a design question and its recorded answer.

  · CONFIDENTIALITY, WHICH INVERTS THE REVERSE CHANNEL. The permit case sent the builder's design back to the publisher and could be public. A bid is competition-sensitive and often proprietary: each bidder's design goes back to the buyer ONLY, and no bidder may see another's. So the reverse channel here needs per-recipient privacy that the forward channel (public requirements) does not. Nothing in reflow2 models who may read a design today.

  · AFTER AWARD, THE GRAPH BECOMES THE CONTRACT BASELINE. The requirements graph plus the winning design is what the contract delivers against; acceptance testing is the Verifications; a change during the contract is a ChangeEvent whose blast radius `propagate_change` already computes. The one graph would carry the thread from solicitation through award to acceptance — the founding chain (requirements → capabilities → verified → fielded) running across the buyer/contractor boundary, which is the organisational split the x-axis node described from Anthony's acquisitions experience.

🛑 THE COUNTERS THIS ADDS, recorded beside the idea:
  · FAIRNESS AND THE RECORD. In public procurement the solicitation text is the legally operative document. If a graph and its prose disagree, the prose governs, and a bidder who built to the graph could be non-compliant. The graph has to be the official publication itself, or be clearly subordinate to it.
  · COMPLIANT IS NOT COMPETITIVE. Accounting for every requirement makes a bid acceptable, not a winner; price, past performance and quality of approach decide awards. A tool that makes compliance easy does not make the rest easier, and must not be sold as if it did.
  · ADOPTION. Nothing suggests sam.gov or any buyer publishes requirements as a graph, and nothing here is a claim that one does or would. As with the city case, the first proof is one solicitation transcribed and one bid designed against it — and a buyer's own requirements (a company's internal RFP) are a far easier first user than a federal portal.

⭐ ONE MECHANISM, THREE SETTINGS NOW: a city publishing code, a standards body publishing a standard, a buyer publishing a solicitation. Each is a publisher who owns the requirements and one or more builders who satisfy them with evidence. The same four gaps recur in all three — a cross-design SATISFIES, evidence that can travel back, a checkable publisher identity, and requirements that apply only under conditions — and procurement adds a fifth: who may read which design.
properties.name: OPEN — is a template, at its simplest, just a PUBLISHED SET OF REQUIREMENTS that somebody else satisfies however they like — "the requirements for a shop in Kennewick, WA" — rather than a seed that copies a field's shape into a new design?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill, after searching first. The search found four close neighbours, all open or parked, and the finding that makes this worth recording separately is that the new framing joins them: the template ideas were about seeding SHAPE, the x-axis idea was about a design that holds only intent, and the environment layer was designed for externally imposed rules using this same city as its worked example. A published requirements template is where all three meet, and the parked vocabulary had been waiting for exactly this kind of real request.

Kept as a new node rather than a sharpening of the seed-template node, because it is a different kind of template (obligations you satisfy, not structure you own), with a different staleness profile and a different mechanism.

Authored by Anthony (who:ajs); the example is his brother's real plan. Nothing about Kennewick's actual code was looked up or is asserted here.
